interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic Dossier — Técnicas Reunidas (TRE.MC) · Industrials / EPC Engineering & Construction

*Eight consecutive quarterly calls, 2024-08-03 → 2026-05-14, cross-referenced against the screener's hard financial trajectory.*

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story over these eight quarters is one of a **post-COVID balance-sheet rehabilitation that succeeded, wrapped in a strategic-transformation narrative ("SALTA") that is still mostly a promise — and which, at the very last call, collided with a live geopolitical shock.**

**Act I — "We will double margins to 8% by 2028" (Aug-2024).** The opening call is pure strategy theater. Chairman Juan Lladó walks through the SALTA strategy's "seven pillars" (services, North America, decarbonization, EPC-with-partners, digitalization, talent) unveiled at the May-2024 Abu Dhabi Capital Markets Day, anchored on one number: *"doubling to 8% … 2028 operating margins."* The thesis is a re-rating from a low-margin, balance-sheet-impaired EPC contractor into a higher-margin, services-led, de-risked engineering partner. Order intake is light (€1.4B H1) but management insists *"it wouldn't be a big challenge to replace 2024 sales."*

**Act II — "The backlog is record and healthy" (Nov-2024 → May-2025).** The emphasis shifts from strategy slides to **commercial proof points**: a record €12.4B backlog (Nov-24), then €12.5B (FY-24), then a step-change to €14.9B (Q1-25) on the €7.3B Lower Zakum award. The recurring refrain becomes *"healthy"* backlog "with a strategic partner" (almost always Sinopec). The de-risking sub-narrative — partnering on EPC to offload execution risk — is consistent and credible.

**Act III — "Services is breaking the glass ceiling" (Aug-2025 → Feb-2026).** The transformation narrative gains its first hard evidence. Services awards reach €333M for FY-25 at *"25% to 30%"* margins (vs ~4% group EPC), 23 new clients, 11 frame agreements. Two new growth legs are *introduced*: (i) **Power** — ambition raised from ~€300M/yr historical to *">€1 billion per year"*, justified by AI/data-center electrification demand, culminating in the **TR Power spin-off** ("before summer"); and (ii) **Digitalization/"Reimagine TR"** — a claim that *"around 60% of the man hours in our sector can be automated"* yielding *"€200 million per year in cost efficiencies."* FY-25 prints the cleanest slide in years: SEPI rescue loan **repaid early (Dec-1-2025)**, dividend resumption announced for 2026, 2026 guidance of >€6.5B sales / >5% EBIT margin / ~€200M net profit.

**Act IV — The shock (May-2026).** The Q1-2026 call is structurally different — management leads with a dedicated **"Middle East conflict"** section. An Iran war has closed the Strait of Hormuz; **two-thirds of backlog is in the Middle East**; four projects "deep inside construction" (~€1.5B of backlog) are materially disrupted; 1,061 shipments affected; a **€45M provision** cuts reported Q1 EBIT from €76M underlying to **€31M**. Simultaneously, management dangles the single most concrete catalyst of the entire series: **€4–8B of awards "most likely before June 13"** (≈45 days out), with *"a very high chance of being awarded around €6 billion."* The arc thus ends on maximum tension: the structural transformation is finally producing numbers, a near-term award catalyst is hard-dated — but the entire backlog's center of gravity sits directly under the oil-shock blast radius.

**Growth drivers quietly dropped / re-weighted:** Decarbonization/hydrogen, the loud headline pillar of 2024, is steadily demoted — by Nov-2025 management concedes *"very few projects have been launched this year"* and earlier admitted the *"hype has disappeared"* (Nov-24). Steel decarbonization, hyped in Aug-24, fades to clients *"moving from hydrogen to carbon capture."* The growth narrative has rotated from **decarbonization → services → power/AI-electrification** — each pivot chasing the prevailing capital-markets theme.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

The hard numbers **corroborate the balance-sheet-repair and revenue-growth story, but expose the "8% margin" transformation thesis as still almost entirely unrealized, and flag a profitability base far thinner than the headline EPS suggests.**

| Management claim | Quarter | The financials say | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Doubling to 8% operating margins by 2028" | Aug-24 (CMD) | FY-25 group EBIT margin **4.5%**; gross margin in screener **4.2% (contracting)**; net margin **2.4%** | **Unproven.** ~half-way at best; the entire re-rating thesis lives in years 2026–2028 that have not happened. |
| Revenue/backlog growth is real | All | Rev **2021 €2.81B → 2025 €6.47B**; +45.3% YoY 2025, 3-yr CAGR +15.2%; backlog €11B→~€15B | **Strongly confirmed.** Top-line growth is the most credible part of the story. |
| EPS/profit inflecting | FY-25 | NI **2021 −€190M → 2025 +€157M**; EPS −3.25 → **+2.01**; +74.8% YoY | **Confirmed directionally**, but off a deeply negative base — this is *recovery*, not secular compounding (EPS 3-yr CAGR **+0.0%**). |
| Services at "25–30%" margin is a margin game-changer | Aug-25→Feb-26 | Services rev only **€254M of €6.47B (~4% of group)**; group margin still 4.5% | **True but immaterial so far.** The high-margin mix is real but too small to move the consolidated needle yet. |
| "Best-ever quarterly EBIT … €64M" / "12th quarter of growth" | Aug-25 | Corroborated by the trajectory; FY-25 EBIT €291M (+61%) | **Confirmed.** |
| Net cash / balance sheet healthy, SEPI repaid | FY-25, Q1-26 | **Net cash −€360M (live, net cash) / −€201M (scan)**; SEPI PPL repaid Dec-25 | **Confirmed — the genuine bright spot.** Real net cash, no leverage problem. |
| 2026 guide: >€6.5B sales, >5% EBIT, ~€200M NI | Feb-26 | Q1-26 *underlying* EBIT €76M (+36%) tracks the >5% path **before** the €45M war provision; **reported** Q1 EBIT €31M, latest-Q EPS YoY **−46%**, **TTM FCF €0** | **At risk.** The underlying run-rate supports the guide; the conflict provision and a zero-FCF TTM directly threaten the FY-26 delivery. |
| Cash converts from EBITDA; "discipline with cash" | Recurring | TTM **FCF €0**; FCF margin **1.9%**; P/FCF **18.4x** | **The soft underbelly.** Management deflects on working capital every single quarter; FCF is structurally weak and lumpy (down-payment-driven), and is currently *zero* on a TTM basis. |

**The two numbers that puncture the bull narrative:** (1) **ROIC 2.2% / gross margin 4.2%** — this is a thin-margin, low-return contractor whose returns on capital do not cover any reasonable cost of capital; the "transformation" must deliver or the stock is a low-quality cyclical. (2) **DCF fair value €22.5 vs price €32.0**, with *every* valuation method showing negative margin of safety (DCF −42%, EPV −30%, Graham −100%, OwnerEarnings −13%, IV15 −100%). On the screener's own models, **TRE.MC is not cheap — it is ~30–40% expensive**, which is a critical and counterintuitive finding for a "deep_value" tag.

**Where the story is RICHER than the numbers:** the Power (€1B/yr) and digitalization (€200M/yr savings) claims — both are pipeline/ambition with essentially zero realized financial footprint in the trajectory. **Where it is POORER than the numbers:** management undersells how genuinely repaired the balance sheet is (real net cash, SEPI gone, equity back above pre-COVID) — the survival risk that justified the depressed multiple has largely been retired.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Trajectory: RISING and increasingly specific from Aug-2024 → Feb-2026, then sharply DEFENSIVE in May-2026.** A clear arc from offensive (growth/strategy) to, at the very end, damage-control.

- **Aug-24 — measured-optimistic, hedged on timing.** *"It wouldn't be a big challenge to replace 2024 sales."* On decarbonization already cautious: *"things are not moving as fast as probably we expected … but I would never say we are negative."* Offensive but with audible hedges.
- **Nov-24 — confident, "record" language.** *"This is not a challenge anymore … record backlog of €12.4 billion."* First overt swagger.
- **Feb-25 — most confident of the series, leads with guidance.** Breaks house convention: *"Usually, guidance is left to the end … this presentation will flow much better if we start disclosing our targets."* Volunteers 2025 AND 2026 ambitions and a **dividend-return** signal. Volunteering forward numbers is a genuine confidence tell.
- **May-25 / Aug-25 — peak operational confidence.** *"12th quarter in a row of growth … always aligned with our previous guidance"*; *"highest ever quarterly EBIT"*; *"we have broken a glass ceiling"* on services.
- **Feb-26 — triumphant.** *"Exceeded all initial expectations … a real inflection point … we have managed to place TR where we wanted TR to be."* SEPI repaid, dividend resuming, spin-off announced.
- **May-26 — abruptly DEFENSIVE.** Language pivots to *"we have to be and we are being prudent and realistic"* (repeated), *"a wide-shot provision of €45 million."* The chairman bristles defensively when pushed on rebuild CapEx: *"it's not a real question … there's not such a big damage."* The shift from "inflection point" to "prudent and realistic" in one quarter is the single most important tonal datapoint in the dossier.

The offensive→defensive rotation is **event-driven (exogenous war), not a slow erosion of the operating story** — an important distinction for the director: the franchise narrative did not crack; an oil shock landed on top of a still-improving business.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Reliability: MEDIUM-HIGH.** Track record over the window is good and improving, with a consistent, *deliberate* conservatism — but the screener's beat-rate (4/7, 57%) and the brand-new war provision keep this out of "High."

- **FY-24 guide (4% margin, replace sales) → delivered:** €4.5B sales, 4.1% margin, backlog €12.5B. **Met.**
- **FY-25 guide (Feb-25: >€5.2B sales, ~4.5% margin) → over-delivered massively:** actual **€6.5B sales (+45%), 4.5% margin, €291M EBIT — "€57M above our initial goal."** A large, clean beat. Management explicitly framed it as exceeding expectations.
- **Sandbagging pattern: YES, and openly admitted.** *"If we see contingencies to be released, we would prefer to retain them until the very end … we are not going to get crazy. We want to be conservative"* (Feb-25). They systematically hold margin contingencies — consistent with the over-delivery and a reason to trust the >5% FY-26 underlying guide.
- **The check against the screener:** earnings beat rate is **4/7 (57%)** — i.e., the over-delivery is real but not metronomic; they have missed roughly 3 of 7 quarters, and **latest-Q EPS came in −46% YoY** under the provision. The conservative-guide habit is a credibility asset; the lumpiness and the fresh provision are why it is Medium-*High*, not High.

**Net:** When management gives a number with the strait open, believe it slightly under-promised. The FY-26 guide (>5% EBIT, ~€200M NI) is credible on the *underlying* run-rate; the binary variable is now exogenous (Hormuz), not managerial.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Three topics recur where analysts press and management *systematically deflects* — and one of them has now bitten.

1. **Working capital & cash flow — the perennial deflection.** Álvaro Lenze (Nov-24, Feb-25), Filipe Leite (multiple), Juan Cánovas (May-26) all push on *why receivables keep climbing* and *what net cash will actually be.* Management's answer never changes: *"if you have bigger sales … the immediate consequence is that you have bigger accounts receivable,"* and *"if I have cash, the cash is for my suppliers … if the cash is for investors, I'm afraid I'm not doing the correct thing."* The CFO repeatedly **refuses to give a year-end cash target** (*"that's a tricky question"*). This is the clearest evasion in the series and maps directly to the **TTM FCF €0 / 18.4x P/FCF** weakness — the one place the financials and the narrative are quietly at odds.
2. **Litigation / disputes (Teesside-KPP Finland, others) — chronic non-answer.** Filipe Leite (Nov-24), and again (May-26) ask for resolution timing; management's stance is fixed: *"I don't think it's correct or sensible to talk about litigations in public,"* softened only to *"we feel comfortable … a large percentage of our disputes will be very much finished this year"* (May-25) and finally a concrete *"final ruling from the arbitrator maybe July"* (May-26). A multi-year overhang that analysts will not let go of.
3. **Turbine supply for the €1B Power ambition — unresolved.** Mick Pickup (Feb-26): *"if you want a turbine … you can have that turbine in 2030. So how does TR get in that queue?"* Management answers with relationship-quality ("the OEMs call us"), **not** with secured slots — a real gap under the most-hyped new growth leg.
4. **Capacity to execute a step-up in awards — pushed repeatedly, answered confidently.** Juan Cánovas (May-25), Ignacio Doménech (May-26) probe whether TR can absorb €4–8B of new awards; here management is *credibly* specific (India headcount 4x in 3 years, ~13,500 staff, satellite offices) — this one is a strength, not an evasion.

**The tell:** every cash/working-capital question is met with philosophy ("discipline," "suppliers first") rather than a number. For a deep-value/expectations-arbitrage thesis, that is the pressure point most likely to disappoint.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

**🔴 RED FLAGS**
- 🔴 **Two-thirds of backlog in the Middle East, into a live Hormuz/oil shock** (May-26). The €45M provision is explicitly conditioned on *"Strait of Hormuz opening in June, no resume of hostilities"* — if hostilities resume, the provision is a floor, not a cap. Maximum single-factor concentration at the worst moment.
- 🔴 **Chronic working-capital opacity + TTM FCF €0** — EBIT grows but cash conversion is repeatedly deflected and is currently nil; the business is structurally down-payment-dependent for cash.
- 🔴 **Altman-Z 1.6 (distress zone) and ROIC 2.2%** — despite net cash, the composite solvency/return profile remains low-quality cyclical, not a fortress.
- 🔴 **Every valuation model says expensive** (DCF €22.5 vs €32.0; all five methods negative MoS) — the "deep_value" label is contradicted by the screener's own DCF/EPV/Graham.
- 🔴 **Decarbonization pillar quietly demoted** — a headline 2024 growth driver shrank to *"very few projects launched"*; narrative rotates to whatever theme is hot (now AI/power).
- 🔴 **Provision-driven −46% latest-Q EPS YoY** — the first real earnings dent of the series, and it is exogenous and potentially recurring.

**🟢 GREEN FLAGS**
- 🟢 **SEPI rescue loan repaid early (Dec-1-2025) → dividend resumption 2026** — the balance-sheet rehabilitation is *complete and verified*, retiring the survival-risk discount.
- 🟢 **Genuine net cash (−€360M live)**, equity restored above pre-COVID — no leverage wall.
- 🟢 **Backlog €11B→~€15B with strategic partners (Sinopec)** — multi-year revenue visibility, execution risk shared.
- 🟢 **Services proving out (€333M awards, 25–30% margins, 23 new clients)** — the highest-margin leg of the thesis is real, just small.
- 🟢 **Conservative-guidance habit validated by a €57M FY-25 over-delivery** — management under-promises.
- 🟢 **Hard-dated near-term catalysts**: €4–8B awards "before June 13," Teesside arbitration ruling "maybe July," TR Power spin-off "before summer," maiden dividend — an unusually dense, dated catalyst cluster.

---

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **Management/voice change mid-series.** From Nov-2025 the chairman is rendered as **"Juan Arburua"** (transcription) leading, and a new IR voice (Antonio Alonso-Muñoyerro) appears, while CFO **Eduardo San Miguel** is the constant. The CFO's 20-year tenure (*"being the CFO of this company for 20 years"*) is the anchor of credibility; his fingerprints are on every cash answer — and every cash deflection.
- **"Healthy" is the tell-word.** Backlog is described as *"healthy"* relentlessly (Nov-24 onward), a deliberate contrast to TR's pre-2021 history of toxic fixed-price losses. The *de-risking-via-partners* message (Sinopec on nearly every megaproject) is the real, under-appreciated structural change — TR is converting from lump-sum-EPC risk-taker to lower-risk partner/services, which is why margins can rise without the old blow-up risk.
- **Spin-off as value-crystallization signal.** **TR Power** spin-off (announced Feb-26, "before summer") with *"fully separated financial accounts"* and its own management/logo is a textbook sum-of-the-parts move — management is explicitly trying to get the market to value the €1B/yr power growth leg separately. On the Q1-26 call they leave the door open to *external capital* for TR Power (*"it will take a couple of years to fully decouple"*). This is the most activist-friendly, structural catalyst in the file.
